items.plain_english: Fertiliser inputs became sharply more expensive after Middle East supply disruption, while the revised subsidy rates did not cover the full increase. Coromandel therefore sold more rupees of product but retained less profit from those sales.
items.financial_link: The filing shows raw-material expense increasing by ₹767.54 crore and standalone PAT falling by ₹131.27 crore year on year. Management identifies input-cost inflation and inadequate subsidy compensation as the main reason for lower profitability; it does not quantify how much of PAT decline came from each raw material.
items.evidence_summary: The official results release attributes the profit decline largely to elevated raw-material costs caused by the Middle East crisis. Management's earnings call names phosphoric acid, ammonia and sulphur, and says NBS subsidy revisions did not fully compensate the increase.
items.source_title: Coromandel Q1 FY27 results release and earnings-call transcript
items.alternative_explanations: The accounting-line increase can also reflect product volume, mix and inventory timing. Those possibilities are not erased; the cause is confirmed because management explicitly linked the quarter's margin pressure to input prices and subsidy insufficiency.
items.what_would_confirm: Track Q2 phosphoric acid, ammonia and sulphur benchmarks, revised NBS rates, fertiliser segment margin and management's quantified cost bridge.
items.decision_boundary: Confirmed explanation of quarterly pressure; not proof that the pressure is temporary, fully priced in, or an investment opportunity.

monitoring_rules.source_requirement: Official company transcript plus independent primary commodity source
monitoring_rules.improvement_meaning: A sustained decline would reduce a major fertiliser input pressure if subsidy and selling prices do not fall faster.
monitoring_rules.deterioration_meaning: A further rise would increase margin pressure unless subsidy or selling-price pass-through compensates it.

monitoring_rules.indicator: NBS subsidy coverage versus input-cost movement
monitoring_rules.source_requirement: Department of Fertilizers notification and verified input basket
monitoring_rules.improvement_meaning: A narrowing compensation gap would improve fertiliser economics.
monitoring_rules.deterioration_meaning: A widening gap would leave more input inflation with the producer.

items.cause: Lower fertiliser volume was a deliberate inventory response
items.plain_english: The company deliberately reduced production and primary fertiliser sales while input markets were volatile. This makes the higher revenue mainly a price-realisation and mix story, not evidence that physical fertiliser demand or volumes grew.
items.financial_link: The official presentation reports manufactured-plus-imported NPK/DAP primary sales falling from 11.0 to 10.1 lakh tonnes, while nutrients-segment sales rose 9%. Management says higher fertiliser realisation contributed to revenue growth.
items.evidence_summary: Management said production was moderated to optimise inventory amid volatile inputs; the official presentation reports NPK/DAP volume down 8.6% year on year.
items.alternative_explanations: Weather-delayed demand and industry supply constraints also influenced volumes, so production discipline should not be read as the only cause of the decline.
items.what_would_confirm: Compare Q2 production, primary sales, point-of-sale demand and closing inventory with input-price movements.
items.decision_boundary: Explains revenue quality and operating choices; does not establish future demand or margin recovery.

monitoring_rules.indicator: NPK and DAP primary sales volume
monitoring_rules.improvement_meaning: Recovery with stable inventory would indicate physical activity is supporting revenue.
monitoring_rules.deterioration_meaning: A further decline would weaken volume support and require demand-versus-discipline attribution.

items.cause: Crop protection partly offset fertiliser weakness
items.plain_english: A healthier crop-protection business softened the damage from fertiliser margins. Its exports, business-to-business sales and product mix improved, showing that the quarter was not weak across every business line.
items.financial_link: Standalone crop-protection revenue rose 20% to ₹870 crore and segment profit rose 44% to ₹159 crore; segment margin improved from 15% to 18%.
items.evidence_summary: The official release and presentation attribute crop-protection growth to exports, B2B sales, improved mix and traction in key technical products.
items.alternative_explanations: One strong quarter may reflect shipment timing or favourable mix. Durability needs further quarters and cash conversion.
items.what_would_confirm: Check export volumes, realisations, order visibility, receivables and crop-protection margin over the next two quarters.
items.decision_boundary: A demonstrated offset in this quarter; not yet proof of a durable company-wide earnings inflection.

monitoring_rules.source_requirement: Official quarterly presentation or segment accounts
monitoring_rules.improvement_meaning: Stable or improving margin with revenue growth would support a durable offset thesis.
monitoring_rules.deterioration_meaning: Margin reversal would suggest the Q1 mix and export benefit was temporary or weakening.

items.cause: Rainfall deficit created a near-term demand risk
items.plain_english: Weak early rainfall delayed sowing and made farmers cautious. That can postpone fertiliser and crop-protection purchases, but the company also reported July rainfall recovery and stronger point-of-sale fertiliser movement, so the final seasonal impact was still uncertain.
items.financial_link: Management reported a 23% rainfall deficit that later moderated to 17%, lower reservoir levels and delayed sowing; point-of-sale fertiliser volume nevertheless increased 13% to 7.9 lakh tonnes.
items.evidence_summary: The earnings call describes rainfall, reservoir, acreage and farmer-sentiment pressure, while explicitly noting subsequent rainfall recovery and mixed crop acreage.
items.alternative_explanations: Channel inventory, product pricing and crop mix can change sales independently of rainfall. The evidence supports risk, not a proven earnings loss attributable to rain.
items.what_would_confirm: Use official rainfall and reservoir updates, crop sowing acreage, point-of-sale volumes and Q2 segment revenue together.
items.decision_boundary: Supported demand risk only; it is not classified as the confirmed cause of Q1 profit decline.

monitoring_rules.collection_instruction: Return only realised or observed all-India rainfall departure/deficit for a completed period. Exclude forecasts, probability ranges, model error, normal-category thresholds and historical LPA baselines.
monitoring_rules.source_requirement: India Meteorological Department primary release; realised observation only, not forecast or model range
monitoring_rules.improvement_meaning: A falling deficit reduces one demand risk but must be checked against regional rain, reservoir and sowing data.
monitoring_rules.deterioration_meaning: A widening deficit raises crop-area and agri-input demand risk.

monitoring_rules.indicator: Relevant crop sowing acreage versus prior year
monitoring_rules.collection_instruction: Return the latest All-India Kharif or Rabi crop-area release with the reporting date, current total area and corresponding prior-year total area. Preserve crop-wise rows; exclude forecasts and commentary without the official table.
monitoring_rules.source_requirement: Ministry of Agriculture release published by Press Information Bureau
monitoring_rules.improvement_meaning: Acreage recovery would support fertiliser and crop-protection demand potential.
monitoring_rules.deterioration_meaning: A sustained acreage decline would increase demand risk, subject to crop and regional mix.
